name: EBITDA
title: EBITDA: Formula, Worked Example and Limits
description: EBITDA means earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization; it is a non-GAAP earnings measure, not cash generated.
definition: EBITDA means earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization; it is a non-GAAP earnings measure, not cash generated.
explanation: EBITDA adds deducted interest, income tax, depreciation and amortization back to net income. For $80,000 net income, $10,000 net interest expense, $20,000 income tax and $30,000 D&A, EBITDA is $140,000. Against $500,000 revenue, the margin is 28%.
formula: EBITDA = net income + net interest expense + income tax expense + D&A; margin = EBITDA / revenue × 100%.
formulaNote: Unadjusted same-period earnings reconciliation in one currency. Signed losses, net-interest income and tax benefits are supported. Operating-income mode includes separately entered other nonoperating income or expense, excluding interest and tax. No cash-flow forecast, valuation or discretionary adjusted-EBITDA addbacks.

example.title: Reconcile net income to a 28% margin
example.intro: net_income: 80000; interest: 10000; income_tax: 20000; depreciation: 20000; amortization: 10000; revenue: 500000
example.assumptions: Unadjusted same-period earnings reconciliation in one currency. Signed losses, net-interest income and tax benefits are supported. Operating-income mode includes separately entered other nonoperating income or expense, excluding interest and tax. No cash-flow forecast, valuation or discretionary adjusted-EBITDA addbacks.

pitfall.title: Keep the model boundary clear
pitfall.text: Do not add D&A twice or confuse operating income with net income. Other nonoperating items can make an operating-income shortcut differ from a net-income reconciliation.

name: Factoring reserve and settlement
title: Factoring reserve and settlement: Formula, Worked Example and Limits
description: A factoring reserve is the part of an invoice’s face value held back from the initial advance and used for the final settlement after fees and collection.
definition: A factoring reserve is the part of an invoice’s face value held back from the initial advance and used for the final settlement after fees and collection.
explanation: A factoring advance is part of the invoice proceeds, not extra revenue. On a $10,000 invoice with an 80% advance, 2% per 30 days prorated for 45 days and $50 other fees, you receive $8,000 today and $1,650 at settlement: $9,650 in total.
formula: Advance = invoice × advance rate; reserve = invoice − advance; signed settlement = reserve − fees; total proceeds = invoice − fees.
formulaNote: One fully collected invoice, one advance today and all fees deducted at collection. Select invoice-face or advance fee base, a constant per-interval rate, prorated or started intervals and separately entered other fees. No default, recourse, upfront deductions, statutory APR, lender quote or financing approval.

example.title: Prorate a 45-day fee interval
example.intro: invoice: 10000; advance_rate: 80; fee_rate: 2; interval: 30; days: 45; billing: Prorated periods; fee_base: Invoice face value; other_fees: 50
example.answer: Total net proceeds: 9,650.00 under these assumptions.
example.assumptions: One fully collected invoice, one advance today and all fees deducted at collection. Select invoice-face or advance fee base, a constant per-interval rate, prorated or started intervals and separately entered other fees. No default, recourse, upfront deductions, statutory APR, lender quote or financing approval.

pitfall.title: Keep the model boundary clear
pitfall.text: Do not add the advance to the entire invoice amount after fees. The advance was already paid out of that invoice. A negative final settlement means more is owed than the held reserve.

name: Average daily balance
title: Average daily balance: Formula, Worked Example and Limits
description: Average daily balance is the sum of daily account balances divided by the number of days in the period; it weights each balance by the days it remains outstanding.
definition: Average daily balance is the sum of daily account balances divided by the number of days in the period; it weights each balance by the days it remains outstanding.
explanation: Average daily balance weights each daily balance by how long it lasts. A $500 balance for 9 days, $700 for 10 days and $400 for 11 days totals 15,900 balance-days. Over 30 days, the average is $530; at 24% / 365, estimated simple interest is $10.45.
formula: ADB = sum(balance × days) / cycle days; simple interest estimate = max(ADB, 0) × APR / year basis × cycle days.
formulaNote: Single-balance, inclusive-date or consecutive segment worksheet. Posting-day changes count that day and same-day changes combine. Signed credit balances are retained. Optional simple interest uses max(ADB, 0), one entered APR and a 360/365 divisor; no grace periods, daily compounding, multiple APR buckets or exact issuer bill.

example.title: Weight a purchase and payment by posting date
example.answer: Average daily balance: 530.00 under these assumptions.
example.assumptions: Single-balance, inclusive-date or consecutive segment worksheet. Posting-day changes count that day and same-day changes combine. Signed credit balances are retained. Optional simple interest uses max(ADB, 0), one entered APR and a 360/365 divisor; no grace periods, daily compounding, multiple APR buckets or exact issuer bill.

pitfall.title: Keep the model boundary clear
pitfall.text: A simple average of three balance amounts ignores their duration. Posting dates, grace periods and separate APR categories can make a card issuer’s bill differ from a single-balance simple-interest estimate.

name: Construction loan draw
title: Construction loan draw: Formula, Worked Example and Limits
description: A construction loan draw is an advance of part of a construction commitment as funds are released; undrawn commitment is not the same as principal already borrowed.
definition: A construction loan draw is an advance of part of a construction commitment as funds are released; undrawn commitment is not the same as principal already borrowed.
explanation: Construction interest depends on funds actually drawn. With $50,000 drawn November 1 and another $50,000 November 16, the average outstanding balance for November is $75,000. At 12% on an actual/365 basis, 30 days cost $739.73 before separately paid fees.
formula: Interval interest = actual principal outstanding × annual rate × actual days / 360 or 365; total interest = sum(interval interest).
formulaNote: Constant-rate, interest-paid-separately construction period with dated nonnegative draws, opening principal and a commitment ceiling. Includes draw day and final day; actual calendar days divided by chosen 360/365. No principal repayments, interest capitalization, land equity, approval or permanent mortgage stage.

example.title: Two draws across a 30-day construction period
example.answer: Total construction interest: 739.73 under these assumptions.

Includes draw day and final day; actual calendar days divided by chosen 360/365. No principal repayments, interest capitalization, land equity, approval or permanent mortgage stage.

pitfall.title: Keep the model boundary clear
pitfall.text: Do not charge a full month of interest on the entire approved commitment when only part has been advanced. Interest reserves and capitalized interest require a separate model.
